title: Seat a hot-swap drive carrier with its cam handle
instruction: Slide the blue drive carrier fully into the grey bay with its orange handle open, then swing the handle closed across the carrier's front until it latches, so the drive stays seated.
context: Replacing hot-swap drives is routine server work (O*NET 49-2011.00, 15-1231.00): the carrier goes in with its handle open, and closing the handle levers it into the connector and latches it. Unlike board tasks where the robot moves the part directly, here it has to operate a hinged lever on the part, in the right order.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Drive bay: grey PLA, 2.5 kg, open top, 14.6 x 8.6 cm footprint, mouth facing the arms at x 30, centred at y -15. It has a 0.4 cm floor, low side walls 2 cm tall with a 7.2 cm wide channel between them, a 0.6 cm back wall at 14 cm from the mouth, and a dark grey catch post (1 x 0.8 x 3.8 cm) at the mouth on the left. Drive carrier: blue PLA, 300 g, 12 x 7 x 2.2 cm, in the channel with its front face 4 cm out of the mouth. A spring plunger (2.4 x 1 cm, 0.8 N per mm, 0.9 cm travel) sticks 1.9 cm out of its rear. Handle: orange PLA bar, 9.1 x 1 x 0.8 cm, 30 g, 1 mm above the carrier's top on a vertical pin 0.6 cm behind its front face and 1 cm in from its left side. The bar reaches 7.5 cm in front of the pin, where a 1.2 x 1.2 x 2.7 cm pull tab stands on it, and 1.6 cm behind the pin (the hook). It starts open, pointing straight at the arms.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a protractor on a top photo. f is the carrier's front face, positive inside the bay's mouth. 0 if the bay ever moved 2 cm or turned 10 degrees, or the carrier was lifted 1.2 cm off the bay floor or tilted 15 degrees. Otherwise: 1.0 if at the end the carrier is seated (f at least 0.7 cm) with the handle shut (at least 85 degrees from open), steady to 1 mm for 1 s; 0.75 if the handle reached 45 degrees with f at least -0.8 cm (hook behind the post); 0.5 if f ever reached 0.7 cm; 0.25 if f reached -0.8 cm while the handle was under 30 degrees; else 0.
reset_notes: Press the handle's latch, swing the handle fully open (pointing at the arms), and slide the carrier back until its front face is 4 cm outside the bay's mouth, centred in the channel. Put the bay back on its marked outline.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes. The handle is a revolute joint, the connector a prismatic joint with a spring drive. The hook levers the carrier by contact with the post alone. Below 85 degrees the handle's drive holds it where it was left (like a stiff hinge). From 85 degrees it latches and is driven into its 90-degree stop. The bay is heavy (2.5 kg). No contact force cap is enforced in simulation.
